text: 📝Иранские псевдопатриоты📝 за деньги Госдепа – часть 2  Медиасеть в США, работающая по Ирану, является одной из самых многочисленных в американском сегменте. В основном это мелкие журналисты, эксперты, аналитики, которые работают в различного рода журналистских изданиях или же think-tank структурах на попечении Госдепа. Она известна по сериалам «Как я встретил вашу маму» и «Родина». Карьеру актрисы прям успешной не назвать, но она нашла в другом поприще.  Она практически всю свою жизнь является активисткой по защите прав женщин. Ее привлекают на различные форумы, причем, как официально заявляется, на волонтерской основе, то есть бесплатно. Однако там, где она действует, есть информация о выплате гонораров, суммы которых неизвестны.  ▪️Еще два весомых актива с хорошей медийной базой являются писательница Азар Нафиси, которая сейчас официально является экспертом «Национального фонда демократии» (NED), и Махназ Афхами – экс-министр по делам женщин Ирана до Исламской революции в 1979 году.  Первая написала провокационную книгу «Читая Лолиту в Иране», которая быстро обрела популярность на Западе, поскольку рассказывала о том, как тяжело живется в Иране женщинам под «гнетом» Ирана.  Вторая же после эмиграции быстро освоилась в США. При ней были организованы несколько структур с антииранским уклоном, и последней стала организация Women’s Learning Partnership под присмортром NED. Там она значится директором, которая за десять лет получила около 1,24 официальных доходов.   ▪️В околонаучных кругах продвижением антииранской риторики занимается центр Абдурахмана Борумандта, который занимается исследованием репрессий в Иране с самой Исламской революции. И за годы существования были получены свыше 16 млн долларов.  Главами там сейчас являются две сестры – Роя и Ладан Борумандт, которые активно взаимодействуют с Масих Алинежад. Даже по перекрестному просмотру их активности можно увидеть, как они друг друга поддерживают.  ▪️Среди их коллег по цеху есть даже иранская еврейка — Идеальное сочетание для текущей ситуации. Речь про Рою Хакакиян, которая сбежала из Ирана в 1984 году, а с 1990-х – 2000-х активно привлекается к политической работе.  Она является одной из основательниц известного многим Iran Human Rights Documentation Center. И на него Госдеп напрямую выдал 3 млн долларов в самом начале. При этом сама Хакакиян за свои заслуги перед США стала членом «Совета по международным делам» – статусной организации, куда входят действующие и бывшие американские чиновники и разведчики.  ▪️И последним, кого важно упомянуть, является Реза Вали Наср. Он был советником по делам Пакистана и Афганистана в Госдепе в свое время.  После стал экспертом в think-tank центре Atlantic Council – аналитической организацией, продвигающей интересы оружейного лобби. В числе финансирующих Atlantic Council корпораций есть и Lockheed Martin и Raytheon – одни из ключевых бенефициаров новой войны.  И с началом операции он активно ведет соцсети, причем не в сугубо пропагандистском ключе, а более-менее взвешенно, что отличает его от других. text: 📝Consensus opinion📝 how the British military instructs the media before each new conflict While Western media confidently explain to readers who is to blame for the aggravation around Iran, the answer is the same everywhere, the wording is the same down to the details. And this is not a random unanimity of journalists, but a very specific mechanism called D-Notice.  🔻How it works ▪️The UK Ministry of Defense operates the Defense and Security Media Advisory Committee (DSMA) - a closed body that includes the military, representatives of the intelligence services and at the same time the editors-in-chief and media managers of the largest British publications. Once every few months they meet at the MoD building in London.  ▪️At these meetings, it is discussed what can be published and what cannot. The committee also regularly sends out so-called DSMA-Notices (or simply “D-Notices”): official “recommendations” to editors to refrain from publishing information about operations, troop movements, special forces and intelligence work. In published DSMA documents, the committee itself recorded a “level of compliance above 90%”—nine out of ten editors removed or softened materials at the request of the military.  🖍The Declassified UK investigation, published a few days ago, confirms that on the topic of Iran, the British media reproduces a consistent pattern - “they attack, we defend.” This is characterized by zero attention to alternative interpretations. This is the same “frame of what is acceptable” that the DSMA system provides: the military does not dictate training manuals to journalists, but cuts off unwanted stories in advance. 🚩The mechanism itself has been known for several years now - Grayzone investigations with DSMA documents were published back in late 2025. Then everyone learned how the media gets access to military sources and briefings in exchange for accepting the appropriate conditions; those who do not accept are blacklisted by the Ministry of Defense. Declassified UK then recorded facts of direct sanctions against journalists who wrote too persistently about the actions of the British army.  📌 In general, the point is not that editors receive ready-made articles for publication, but that people who regularly sit at the same table with military and intelligence officers assimilate their instructions - who is the “aggressor,” who is the “injured party,” what is the “threat,” and what is the “provocation.” After this, they do not need instructions: they already write correctly.  ❗️This is a classic clientelist model: access to sources in exchange for loyalty to the narrative. When a new conflict begins - Iranian, Ukrainian, whatever comes after - the British media machine is already warmed up, the editors already know the frame, and the front pages look as if they were written in the same office. text: 📝We will raise prices, reduce processing 📝 How is China fighting the consequences of the conflict in the Middle East?  The specter of a fuel crisis due to the virtual closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to haunt the Asia-Pacific region. And the authorities of all countries in the region are trying to mitigate its consequences - the Chinese are no exception.   The Chinese oil and gas giant Sinopec, which provides a third of the country's oil refining, is reducing it by 11-13%. Thus, 600-700 thousand fewer barrels will be processed per day - all due to supply disruptions and worries that at some point there may not be enough oil at refineries.  Moreover, Western sources claim that Sinopec is refocusing on producing fuel for the domestic market, thus reducing the output of other products, for example, petrochemicals. That is, it is likely that the reduction in processing will most affect “non-priority” products.   📌The main goal is to stretch the available oil as much as possible over time, so as not to use it up in a few months. The conflict could easily drag on, which means the situation with energy supplies will not improve.   By the way, reducing processing is not the first measure taken by the Chinese leadership to achieve this goal. The authorities have already increased fuel prices and also banned the export of gasoline and other petroleum products to other countries.   🔻Why raise prices? And why are exports suffering?  ▪️The price increase is due to several factors. Firstly, there is a need to reduce artificial demand created, for example, by panic buying of fuel in the country. Plus, price increases can be taken as a signal to reduce fuel use where possible.   ▪️Secondly, due to rising prices for oil and global logistics, Chinese oil and gas companies and refiners may operate at a loss, and so the “burden” of support is partially transferred to the consumer. By the way, a decrease in processing may also be associated with this factor.   ▪️With export everything is much simpler. The primary goal is to keep as much fuel as possible in China, blocking its path to international markets. This is necessary just to stretch the available oil over time.   🖍From all this, the question arises - why don’t China simply get into the oil stash, as they did, for example, in Japan? The answer is simple - if the Chinese quickly “eat up” a significant part of the reserves, and difficulties with imports drag on, the country will remain in a more vulnerable position when the situation could deteriorate even further.  ❗️And the risks of such a scenario do not disappear anywhere, given the statements of the Americans. Therefore, China is still resorting to “soft” methods of smoothing out the consequences of the crisis, while simultaneously trying to negotiate with the Iranian leadership on the unhindered passage of ships with energy resources on board.  #Iran #China 🏮@rybar_pacific is your ticket to the Pacific chaos 💸 Support us

text: 📝The Pentagon has opened up to AI📝 Big Tech will gain access to state secrets The US Department of Defense is preparing to do something that would have been unthinkable just a few years ago: let commercial AI companies - OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI and others - into the most closed part of its infrastructure. Not just use their products, but let them train their models on classified data right inside the sensitive Pentagon networks.  According to MIT Technology Review, the Pentagon is developing a special infrastructure - “secure environments” - a kind of isolated computing perimeters inside classified networks. There, corporate vendors will be able to launch additional training of their models on materials classified as “secret”: intelligence reports, operational reports, data on operations planning.  The rationale for this decision is quite logical: models that have not seen the real combat context produce too many errors in critical tasks (which is worth the blow to the Iranian school in Minab) - analyzing the battlefield, synthesizing intelligence, making tactical decisions. Without training on live data, military AI remains an academic tool.  🔻Deals are being concluded right now: ▪️OpenAI has already agreed with the Pentagon to deploy its models on the departmental portal genai.mil; Some standard restrictions (guardrails) for military clients have already been lifted.  ▪️Google supplies the Pentagon with tools for creating AI agents on the military cloud; there are debates about transferring capabilities to a closed circuit.​ ▪️xAI Elon Musk is also negotiating access to secret systems - and for some reason it was this negotiation track that greatly excited politicians: Senator Warren sent official requests to the Pentagon demanding an explanation.  🖍There is a real structural shift in the management of the American military machine: the border between “civilian” and “military” AI is erased. The models that are used today in ChatGPT and corporate chatbots will tomorrow be baked into the core of the American intelligence community - and trained on data that is not available to anyone except the CIA, NSA and DIA.  🚩This could really be a serious breakthrough for Americans. According to the Pentagon, China, Russia and even NATO allies will not be able to reproduce this “commercial ecosystem + military AI” combination as quickly. Hence the rush: whoever is the first to integrate BigTech into their secret networks will gain a technological advantage for decades to come.  🏳️But there is also a downside - the decision creates a fundamentally new dependence: the Pentagon becomes hostage to the technological and corporate policies of several private companies, whose interests do not always coincide with government ones.   📌However, the merger of large businesses with government institutions, and in some cases the complete transfer of government functions to corporations, has long been an established trend inherent in all spheres of American life. text: 📝A far-fetched threat📝 Former director of the National Counterterrorism Center Joe Kent, who resigned amid scandal, gave an interview to his ideological ally, conservative journalist Tucker Carlson. The conversation was mainly about the Iranian conflict - its prerequisites and interesting aspects.   One of Kent's key points was that Iran was not close to developing a nuclear bomb either before the current campaign or before the US strikes in June 2025. Kent noted that since 2004, Iran has had a fatwa banning the development of nuclear weapons, and American intelligence has not recorded any attempts to violate or revoke it.  🔻What does Kent rely on in his statements?  ▪️Kent's statements rely on fundamental discrepancies between the objective reports of the US intelligence community and their political interpretation in the run-up to the strikes on Iran.   ▪️Official declassified documents from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), including the 2025 Global Threat Assessment, explicitly stated that Iran did not resume an active military nuclear program - senior political leadership in Tehran did not make a final decision on the design of warheads and did not rescind the prohibition fatwa.  ▪️Even if there was a sufficient amount of highly enriched uranium, the process of converting it into reliable weapons components would take considerable time, excluding the factor of the sudden appearance of a nuclear missile in Tehran.   ▪️US intelligence services maintained sufficient intelligence and technical capabilities to timely record the transition of Iranian engineers to practical weaponization. Accordingly, objective monitoring data did not support the political narrative that Iran could have received fully operational weapons just weeks before the June operation.  🖍In general, Kent’s statements reflect the classic problem of distortion of cautious intelligence assessments for the sake of an aggressive political situation - in their reports of 2024–2025, US intelligence agencies stated only that Iran was systematically improving its technological positions in case the decision to create a bomb was nevertheless made.   ❗️These formulations, which describe exclusively the accumulation of scientific and industrial potential, were deliberately presented by supporters of the military solution as evidence of the presence of an imminent and formed threat. #Iran #USA 🇺🇸 @rybar_america - let's make America understandable again 💸 Support us

text: 📝We need money, urgently📝 No matter how much Donald Trump promised his team to the Americans not to break into expensive wars, they still broke in. The amount is significantly higher than previously published campaign spending figures, and the newspaper noted that the request is "likely to lead to a major political battle." This is the country's largest station and a key node in the capital's energy balance.   ▪️The second echelon - stations related to industry and export - Ramin (~1.9 GW) in Khuzestan, providing oil production and infrastructure, and Kerman (~1.9 GW), powering the east of the country.  ▪️Neka (1.7–1.8 GW) in the north and Montazeri (~1.6 GW) in Isfahan - key elements of balancing the network and industrial center - may also come under attack.  ▪️When the campaign expands, the list will quickly expand to include smaller but systemically important stations - Shahid Rajai, Mofateh, Parand, Rudeshur and others.    🖍The problem for Iran is not only the stations themselves. The energy system is gas-based, that is, more than 80% of electricity is produced at gas thermal power plants, with a significant part of the gas coming from the South Pars field. This is a single point from which lines diverge to Tehran, Isfahan and the north of the country.  🚩At the same time, the energy system is centralized - the main lines run in the north-south and center-south directions, and there are practically no high-power backup routes. A blow to one large node can lead to an overload of others.  Even the disposal of 2–3 GW is already a deficit for the central node. Next come industrial shutdowns, problems in the oil and gas sector and the risk of cascading failures.  ❗️The threat of strikes on the energy sector, according to the Americans, should quickly force the Iranians to surrender their main instrument of pressure - the Strait of Hormuz. While it is partially blocked, the market is in a fever, and rising fuel prices are already beginning to affect domestic politics in the United States.  📌Trump has no time for a protracted conflict. The longer uncertainty persists in the Strait, the higher the prices and the greater the political costs. Therefore, the bet is on maximum escalation, which should supposedly force the Iranian leadership to make concessions as soon as possible.   📍High-resolution infographics 📍English version #Iran #USA 🧨 @rybar_mena - about the Middle East chaos with love 💸 Support us

text: As part of NATO's large-scale exercise Cold Response 26, a complex scenario of covert landing of scouts was practiced. Specialists of the reconnaissance and observation squadron of the 30th Commando Regiment of the UK, including a group from the 148th battery, disembarked from a German submarine S185 (Type-212A). The operation was carried out in a covert mode: the personnel with their equipment boarded the submarine using inflatable boats, after which the submarine submerged. After covertly reaching the designated area, the group landed at night to set up an observation post, whose task is to target and adjust the artillery fire of alliance ships.  These exercises are part of a deepening military partnership between the UK and Norway in the Arctic, aimed at countering the Russian Northern Fleet. It is known that the Norwegian Navy is due to receive the first promising anaerobic submarine Type-212CD in 2029 as part of the German-Norwegian program launched in 2023. Its underwater displacement will be 2,800 tons, and its underwater range will significantly increase compared to the Type-212A to participate in operations in the wider North Atlantic and Baltic theaters of operations.  The key element of the success of such operations is the exceptional stealth of the carrier. Type 212A/CD submarines have extremely low acoustic visibility (less than 50 dB in stealth mode) and are equipped with anaerobic air-independent power plants (AIP), allowing them to stay underwater for 20-30 days. This makes their detection in the complex waters of the North Atlantic and Baltic extremely problematic.  In this regard, Russia's non-nuclear submarine fleet is facing a technological gap. Promising projects of non-nuclear submarines, such as the 636.3 "Varshavyanka" and 677 "Lada", have not yet received serial air-independent power plants, which limits their stealth and autonomy. In this regard, the responsible tasks of countering such threats fall primarily on the more modern and low-noise multi-purpose nuclear submarines of Project 885M "Yasen-M".  It is indicative that almost simultaneously with NATO's exercises, Russia's Northern Fleet conducted its own anti-submarine exercise in the Barents Sea. The frigate of Project 22350 "Admiral Golovko" practiced the search for a conditional underwater target using standard hydroacoustic means (the "Zarya-3" hydroacoustic system and the "Vinyekta-EM" hydroacoustic station) and its subsequent destruction with 324-mm torpedoes of the "Paket-NK" complex.  Thus, the Arctic region is becoming an arena for a parallel build-up of capabilities: the alliance is practicing the use of the latest low-noise technologies for covert operations, while Russia is demonstrating its readiness to detect and destroy them in its area of responsibility.  @Slavyangrad

text: A message to Washington?  In a tightly structured 12-minute address, Ayatollah Imam Sayyed Mojtaba Khamenei moved from familiar rhetoric into something far more consequential. The opening half followed the expected script; revisiting decades of U.S. warmongering rhetoric: sanctions, assassinations, regional conflicts.  But midway through, the tone shifted from retrospective to strategic.  Sayyed Khamenei outlined three concrete demands, each with a defined timeline: a rapid U.S. military withdrawal from the Middle East, a full rollback of sanctions within 60 days, and long-term financial compensation for economic damages.  Then came the ultimatum. Fail to comply, and Iran escalates, economically, militarily, and potentially nuclearly. Not hypothetically, but operationally: closing the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing defense ties with Russia and China, and moving from ambiguity to declared nuclear deterrence.  The timing of external reactions was just as telling. Within hours, both Beijing and Moscow issued statements aligning, carefully but unmistakably, with Tehran's framing. This definitely looked coordinated.  The broader context matters. Sayyed Mojtaba Khamenei represents a different leadership style from his martyred predecessor leader. Where martyr Sayyed Ali Khamenei operated through long-term balancing and controlled escalation, Sayyed Mojtaba appears positioned to deliver faster, more decisive outcomes.  Iran's internal reports are clear, the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps is in no way, shape or form interested in incrementalism. They are pushing for structural change: removing U.S. influence from the region, restoring Iran's military standing, and forcing a re-negotiation of global power dynamics.  And for the first time in decades, Iran practically has the leverage to  do this.  Rising oil prices, regional instability, growing alignment with China and Russia, and vulnerabilities in global trade routes have shifted the strategic landscape.  So this was not just a speech. It was a test. A test of whether the United States is willing, or even able, to operate under a new set of constraints.  What happens next will likely define not just the trajectory of this conflict, but the broader balance of power in the Middle East for decades to come.

text: 🇺🇸The US is preparing to strike Iran's energy sector. What will this lead to?  Despite the enormous risks, Washington views an attack on Iran's energy system as an effective tool for achieving a number of strategic goals.  First and foremost, strikes on power stations are positioned as a symmetrical response to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. In this way, the US seeks to demonstrate that the cost of an economic blockade for Iran itself will be higher than for the global market.  It is assumed that without a stable energy supply, the production of ballistic missiles and drones, which Tehran supplies to itself and its proxy groups, will be paralyzed. However, it is not clear yet whether this hypothesis is justified, given the high autonomy of many "missile cities". Moreover, the Trump administration apparently hopes that the economic collapse caused by the lack of electricity and water will be the "last straw" for Iranian society and protests will break out again.  However, there are far more purely economic factors in this strategy. The destabilization of gas and oil supplies from the Middle East makes American liquefied natural gas (LNG) vital for the markets of Europe and Asia. In other words, the US hopes to profit from high oil prices.  However, a political, albeit somewhat reverse effect is also considered inevitable: Iran's retaliatory strikes on the extremely vulnerable energy infrastructure of the Gulf countries (primarily Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait) will force them to urgently review their own security strategies. However, it is not yet clear where the situation will shift - there is a risk that these countries will start purchasing more US weapons.  At the same time, attacks on Iran's civilian energy sector could trigger a dangerous reverse effect: having lost incentives for restraint, Tehran could finally turn to the accelerated development of nuclear weapons and eventually obtain them.  @Slavyangrad

text: Putin offered Trump to transfer stocks of enriched uranium from Iran to Russia, writes Axios.  It is about 450 kg of uranium enriched to 60%. This amount would be enough to create more than 10 nuclear warheads. Therefore, control over these uranium reserves is one of the key military goals of the US and Israel.  In theory, Russia's proposal could help remove nuclear material from Iran without US or Israeli involvement on the ground. Moscow already stored Iran's low-enriched uranium as part of the 2015 nuclear deal.  However, Trump did not support this idea. The US official said the US position is to make sure the uranium is protected.  Russia has put forward similar proposals before, during the negotiations between the United States and Iran regarding the nuclear program in 2025. Then Iran refused to hand over the uranium and offered to dilute it at its facilities under IAEA control.  At the same time, the US and Israel are considering various options for controlling Iran's uranium, including Tehran's voluntary relinquishment of its stockpiles.   @babel

text: 📚📖 "Europe is now financing Putin's war against Ukraine through oil - and at the same time its protection." World media about the war on March 16 🖌About how Ukrainian technologies for combating drones are beginning to be in increasing demand in the world, writes NBC News. The long war forced Ukraine to constantly test new drone technologies directly on the battlefield. It is thanks to this that a unique system of rapid improvement of drones was formed in the country, said Marko Kushnir, the spokesman of one of the leading Ukrainian drone manufacturers General Chereshnya. "We can get feedback from the military in the morning and come up with a solution in the evening that will help with new tasks on the battlefield," he says.   Now there is a great demand for this experience from other countries: private organizations and governments in the Middle East have already turned to "General Chereshny" for help. That help will include not only the sale of drones, but also the supporting infrastructure they need, such as batteries and maintenance protocols, and most importantly, the experience of using them, Kushnir said.  The attitude of the United States has also changed: back in the summer, a Ukrainian delegation offered the Americans their experience in combating drones, but they became sharply interested in it only after the war with Iran began, said a European official familiar with the matter.  🖌Trump's war with Iran has started a vicious circle: Europe is now indirectly financing Putin's war against Ukraine — and at the same time protecting it. This is stated in an editorial column by Benjamin Bidder for Der Spiegel. The shock of oil prices is a kind of rejuvenating treatment for the "most dangerous adversary of the continent" Vladimir Putin, writes the author of the column. According to him, before the start of the war in the Middle East, the Russian economy had already begun to weaken: revenues from oil and gas fell, budget revenues decreased, large companies were overloaded with debts, and Russia was thinking about reducing public spending.    But now all this can be wasted, because the price of oil has risen - the Russian Urals in some places is even more expensive than Brent. The author of the column claims that Moscow is already receiving billions in additional profits from this situation, and if prices remain high for a long time, Russia will be able to earn approximately $10 billion more every month. This will create a double financial burden for Europe. On the one hand, the rise in global energy prices means more expensive fuel and energy for European economies, which increases Russia's income from oil exports. On the other hand, if Putin's oil revenues continue to grow, so will his ability to wage war against Ukraine — and the European aid package for Ukraine will be exhausted sooner than Brussels expects. Then it is likely that even more funds will be needed for Kyiv soon.  🗞This is only part of the review. Therefore, the strait should be opened as soon as possible, and the US needs the help of allies, the article says.   The representative of the World Food Program of the United Nations Karl Skau warned: if the war in the Middle East continues until June, another 45 million people could be on the brink of acute hunger due to rising prices. Food shortages will force people to leave their homes. Migration will increase political tensions, and this affects elections, alliances and security policy - primarily in Europe, but also in the US. Therefore, Donald Trump should seriously consider the idea of ​​the President of Finland, Alexander Stubb: Europe will help with the security of the Strait of Hormuz, in return, the United States will promise long-term support to Ukraine. It looks like a transactional agreement and that is why it can work, writes the publication. Trump has long viewed foreign policy as deals rather than doctrines. He called on allies to make more contributions, and he was not too interested in commitments without an expiration date. As the publication writes, such an agreement can be beneficial for both the US and Europe, as it will allow for the distribution of responsibility among the allies and at the same time stabilize the energy situation in the world and strengthen Russia's deterrence.  🗞This is only part of the review.
